Zeolites are frequently used as catalytic materials because 
of their strong affinity and selectivity for polar compounds 
like H2S (Kulawong et al., 2022). Zeolites are microporous 
crystals with three-dimensional SiO4 and AlO4 tetrahedra 
structures (Kulawong et al., 2022; Bahraminia et al., 2020). 
Among the variously studied zeolites, NaX zeolite and its 
ion-exchanged forms have been extensively utilized for 
H2S removal (Kulawong et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2022). 
To remove sulfur compounds in gas pipelines, it has been 
demonstrated that silver (Ag) exchanged zeolites are effec-
tive adsorbents with a high capacity and absorptivity (Ku-
lawong et al., 2022). Zeolites are good adsorbents for gas 
separation applications because of their large surface area, 
uniform pore diameter, and large number of cationic acti-
ve sites (Bahraminia et al., 2020).

chemicals with low biotoxicity and capable of conversion 
the lignocellulosic biomass to ethanol and lipid, and acti­

(•OH) are commonly employed in hydrolysis stage of 
anaerobic digestion [3, 26, 40, 41]. Table  1 summarizes 
the effects of using different chemical addition on the BMP 
potential and corresponding microbial dominance in anaer­
obic digestion. According to Table 1, different chemicals 
including combined Ca (OH)2 and Urea, three-dimensional 
iron-carbon, combined CaO2, zero-valent iron, combined 
potassium ferrate (PF) and peroxymonosulfate (PMS), 
Glycerin and H2O2 have been used to both improved 
BMP and microbial community. For instance, Rodríguez-
Abalde et al. (2019), reported that addition the Glycerin 
to anaerobic digestion fed with Pig manure improved the 
BMP to 507 mLCH4/gVS [42]. In addition, as summarized 
in Table 1, the results indicated that Methanobacterium and 
Methanosaeta are the dominant archaea in different anaero­
bic reactors assisted with chemical addition as pretreatment 
process. As per the results, it can be concluded that meth­
ane production in anaerobic reactors assisted with chemi­
cal addition as pretreatment follows both hydrogenotrophic 
and acetotrophic methanogenic pathways. For instance, 
Methanobacterium as strictly hydrogenotrophic methano­
gens with capable of methane production via utilizing the 
both hydrogen and carbon dioxide was reported as the dom­
inant methanogens in anaerobic reactors assisted with com­
bined Ca (OH)2 and urea, CaO2, and zero-valent iron (ZVI) 
[26, 39, 40]. Furthermore, in anaerobic reactors utilizing a 
three-dimensional iron-carbon pretreatment process, Meth­
anosaeta, known for its ability to metabolize acetate by 
reducing methyl carbon and oxidizing carboxyl into CO2, 
was identified as the predominant acetotrophic methanogen 
[41]. However, according to Table 1, the dominant bacteria 
in this content are variable. For instance, Xiang Zheng et al. 
(2022) reported Mesotoga as the most dominant bacteria in 
anaerobic reactor fed with black liquor and assisted with 
three-dimensional iron-carbon [41]. Mesotoga is known as 
a typical bacterium in anaerobic reactors and capable of 
enhancing the fermentation and hydrolysis of recalcitrant 
substances like aromatic compounds [43]. While Clos­
tridium with ability to crystalline cellulose degradation and 
TVFA production [44] were reported as dominant bacteria 
in anaerobic reactor assisted with CaO2 and zero-valent 
iron (ZVI) pretreatment [40].
